title: Swiatek Is Out. There Is No Former Champion Left at the French Open.
excerpt: Marta Kostyuk beat the four-time Roland Garros winner 7-5, 6-1 on her 25th birthday. With Gauff, Sinner, Djokovic, and Alcaraz all gone, the 2026 French Open will crown a first-time champion.
body:
Iga Świątek turned twenty-five on Sunday. She celebrated by losing.

The four-time French Open champion was beaten 7-5, 6-1 by Ukraine's fifteenth seed Marta Kostyuk in the fourth round at Roland Garros, extending the most chaotic Grand Slam in recent memory into territory that even the most imaginative scriptwriter would have rejected as implausible.

## The Last Champion Falls

Świątek had not looked entirely comfortable in Paris this fortnight, but she had won her first three matches without dropping a set. There was a sense that the Pole, who has owned this tournament like few players in the Open Era, was quietly working her way into form.

Kostyuk had other plans. The Ukrainian, unbeaten on clay in 2026 with titles in Rouen and Stuttgart, dismantled the former world number one with a performance that mixed relentless baseline defence with devastating forehand winners. She broke Świątek's serve six times. She hit six aces. She ran down shots that most players would not have reached.

"I'm still in shock," Kostyuk said on Court Philippe Chatrier. "To beat such an unbelievable player, who won four times here."

The first set was tight. Both players traded breaks twice, and Świątek held a 5-4 lead with a chance to serve it out. But a double fault and a shanked forehand handed the game back. Kostyuk broke again at 6-5, sealing the set with a backhand crosscourt winner that kissed the line.

The second set was not a contest. Świątek broke to lead 1-0, then won just one more game. Kostyuk rattled off six straight, closing the match with a fizzing return that left Świątek flat-footed at the baseline. The four-time champion briefly left the court between sets; when she returned, the match was already over in all but the scoreboard.

## A Tournament Without Precedent

The 2026 French Open has now lost every former champion in both draws. Novak Djokovic fell to João Fonseca in the second round, coming back from two sets down only to lose in five. Defending women's champion Coco Gauff was upset by Anastasia Potapova. Men's world number one Jannik Sinner lost to Juan Manuel Cerúndolo. Carlos Alcaraz, the 2024 champion, withdrew before the tournament with an injury.

And now Świątek, who had won four of the last five French Open titles and whose record on Philippe Chatrier clay was the most dominant of any active player, is out in the fourth round.

For the first time in the Open Era, Roland Garros will guarantee a first-time champion in both the men's and women's draws.

## What It Means for the NRI Tennis Fan

Indian diaspora fans who set alarms for late-night Grand Slam broadcasts — Roland Garros matches start at 6:30 PM IST on Star Sports — are watching a tournament that has torn up its script. Aryna Sabalenka, the world number one, is now the overwhelming favourite on the women's side. On the men's side, Alexander Zverev, Casper Ruud, and Felix Auger-Aliassime lead a draw that feels startlingly open.

Kostyuk's run has been the story of the clay season. The twenty-three-year-old has not lost a match on the surface in 2026. Her unbeaten streak now stands at sixteen matches. She will face either Elina Svitolina or Belinda Bencic in the quarter-finals.

For Świątek, it was her fourth career defeat at Roland Garros. Her clay court aura, built across four titles in five years, has not vanished — but it has been punctured. At twenty-five, she remains one of the most accomplished players of her generation. But on this birthday, on this court, she was second best.

## What's Next

The quarter-finals begin on Tuesday. Sabalenka faces either Mirra Andreeva or Sorana Cîrstea. Kostyuk awaits the winner of Svitolina-Bencic. On the men's side, Ruud takes on Fonseca — the Brazilian teenager who knocked out Djokovic — in what could be the match of the tournament.

The 2026 French Open has lost its way, or perhaps found a new one. There will be a champion nobody expected.
author: Diaspora Desk
